about: The state officeholder's day (OFFICE-STATE): how a session week, the interim and the governor's year are laid out where a place's own data says nothing more exact. Each place's session windows come from data/research/laws/state-session-calendars.json; per diem from state-legislator-per-diem.json; the line-item veto from state-line-item-veto.json.

sessionWeek.source: What a weekday in session is for a member, Monday to Friday. Most legislatures hold floor sessions and committee meetings Tuesday through Thursday and members travel home and work the district on Monday and Friday (NCSL, 'Legislative Session Length' and 'Legislative Calendars' pages; Rosenthal, 'Heavy Lifting', 2004).
sessionWeek.spread: two to five floor days a week; full-time legislatures (California, New York, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Massachusetts, Wisconsin, Illinois, Ohio, New Jersey) sit more days

committeeMeetsBeforeFloor.source: Standing committees meet on floor days, before or after the floor sits (NCSL, 'Committee Meeting Schedules'). 1 means a committee member's floor day holds a committee meeting.

caucusWeekday.source: Party caucuses meet at the start of the legislative week, before the first floor session (NCSL, 'Legislative Caucuses'). Monday is 1.

interimCommitteeDayOfMonth.source: Interim committees meet about once a month between sessions (NCSL, 'Interim Committees'); the day of the month stands in for each body's own schedule.

stateOfTheStateDaysAfterConvening.source: Governors give the State of the State at or within days of the regular session's opening (NGA, 'State of the State addresses', 2024 and 2025 dates).

budgetProposalDaysAfterConvening.source: Governors submit the executive budget to the legislature at or shortly after the session's opening; statutory deadlines run from before convening to about a month in (NASBO, 'Budget Processes in the States', 2021, table 2).

leadersWeekday.source: The weekday a governor meets the legislature's leaders during session; real governors' schedules vary. Monday is 1.

attendanceDuty.source: How much a member's sense of the job pulls toward showing up for a session, a committee or a caucus, beside their traits' lean (a -1 to 1 term). Real attendance on recorded votes runs well above 90 percent (GovTrack missed-vote rates; state roll-call records), so duty outweighs most temperaments.

officeHoursDuty.source: How much a member's sense of the job pulls toward holding district office hours on a district day, beside their traits' lean. District offices are open most weekdays, but a member is there in person less than on the floor.

meetingHours.source: Hours a member spends with the other members at a caucus or a committee meeting, the time together their tie gains.

stateOfTheStateTopics.source: How many policy questions a State of the State takes up as calls to act; real addresses name a handful of priorities (NGA summaries of 2024 and 2025 addresses).

holdMinute.source: Morning office-day stop; same 9 a.m. day boundary as the shared daytime meeting.

leaderRequestPartyWeight.source: How much a floor leader's party loyalty weighs in answering a member's request to schedule a hearing: a member of the leader's own party gets it, one of the other side loses it. Larger than the tie and trait terms, so a request from the other side is refused unless a deep tie and the leader's traits outweigh it.

leaderRequestTieWeight.source: How much the leader's closeness to the member (their tie today, 0 to 1) adds to granting the request.

clemencyReviewWeekday.source: The weekday a governor takes up one clemency case (Thursday is 4): a governor works through petitions on a regular day each week rather than daily; no dataset in the repository measures it.

clemencyReviewMonths.source: Months before a denied petition is reviewed again: pardon and commutation boards and governors commonly bar a repeat application for a year after a denial (Collateral Consequences Resource Center, state pardon profiles).

clemencyBar.source: The share of a term a person has served that, with a neutral temperament, tips a governor to grant clemency: commutations go overwhelmingly to people far into long terms. A trait lean moves it either way; no dataset in the repository measures it.
